output.answer: As of late 2026, eBay's main competitors are the giant generalist e-commerce marketplaces — above all Amazon, which eBay's own FY2025 Form 10-K names first among large ecosystem rivals alongside Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Apple and Meta — plus Walmart Marketplace and the fast-growing low-price Chinese platforms Temu and AliExpress. eBay's 10-K also flags specialist marketplaces focused on narrow categories (e.g. Etsy, Whatnot, Wayfair, StockX-type niche players), social/shopping channels such as Facebook Marketplace, Instagram and TikTok Shop, and multi-channel tools like Shopify as alternatives pulling buyers and sellers away. Independent U.S. market sizing (Marketplace Pulse, March 2026) puts Amazon far ahead at roughly $300 billion in third-party GMV — about seven times eBay's $39 billion, which still ranks eBay second among U.S. marketplaces — with Temu (~$22B), TikTok Shop (~$15B) and Walmart Marketplace (~$15B) bunched together as the next tier of challengers.
caveats: eBay's 10-K describes competition by category (large ecosystems, specialist marketplaces, social/live commerce, local platforms) and names companies only as examples — the ranking of 'main competitors' is analyst judgment layered on that disclosure.
Marketplace Pulse GMV figures are U.S.-only estimates (Amazon ~$300B, eBay ~$39B, Temu ~$22B, TikTok Shop and Walmart ~$15B each) and may differ from company-reported global numbers.

ECDB's 'Match Score' similarity ranking is one algorithmic configuration the site itself warns 'may not match how you define competition'; it omits important rivals like Etsy and AliExpress-adjacent specialty players.
Market share and GMV shift quickly in e-commerce; figures as of the March 2026 report and FY2025 filings may have changed by the time this is read.

passages.quote: •We may not be able to engage consumers as effectively as our large competitors with broad ecosystems – Some of our competitors, such as Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Amazon, Apple and Meta (Facebook and Instagram), are larger than we are, have greater resources, have a dominant and secure position in other industries or certain significant markets, or offer other goods and services and product ecosystems to consumers and merchants that we do not offer, which can drive consumers to, and keep them locked-in to, their platforms instead of using ours.

•We may not keep up with seller expectations – Consumers and merchants that sell goods on our platforms also have many alternatives, including general ecommerce marketplaces, such as Amazon and Alibaba, and more specialized marketplaces that focus on discrete categories of products. Sellers may also choose to sell their goods through alternative channels, such as multi-channel services like Shopify or social media platforms. Consumers and sellers also can create and sell through their own sites and may choose to purchase online advertising instead of using our services or paying for our advertising products.

platforms, such as Facebook Marketplace. These consumers can also turn to shopping-comparison sites, such as Google Shopping, and social networks that enable purchases, such as Instagram and TikTok. Some consumers, including those in younger demographics, may prefer some of these alternative shopping formats to our largely fixed-price listing and traditional auction-style listing formats.

Amazon remains the dominant U.S. marketplace, with an estimated $300 billion in third-party sales, more than seven times eBay’s and roughly 20 times that of the next competitors. Three platforms – Temu, TikTok Shop, and Walmart – now compete in a tight $15-22 billion range, while specialized marketplaces from Wayfair to Whatnot have carved defensible positions serving niches that mass-market platforms struggle to capture.

eBay holds second position at $39 billion after returning to growth by refocusing on enthusiasts and pre-loved fashion rather than competing for new-in-season goods it acknowledged it couldn’t win. The platform accepted a ceiling in exchange for stability, carving out a defensible position Amazon doesn’t particularly want.

Beyond the top five, five more platforms have built billion-dollar marketplaces: Wayfair at $10 billion in home goods, SHEIN’s marketplace at $6 billion (24% of U.S. GMV), Etsy at $6 billion in handmade goods, Whatnot at $6 billion in live auctions, and Target Plus at $1 billion with its curated model. The marketplace economy is bigger and more diverse than ever.

*   [temu.com](https://ecdb.com/resources/sample-data/retailer/temu) tops the stores most similar to Ebay's biggest store at a 87.3 Match Score and a US$29 AOV.
*   [walmart.com](https://ecdb.com/resources/sample-data/retailer/walmart) is a close alternative at a 82.7 Match Score and a US$95 AOV.
*   [amazon.com](https://ecdb.com/resources/sample-data/retailer/amazon) follows at a 81.1 Match Score and a US$73 AOV.

output.question: Who are eBay's main competitors?

key_facts.fact: eBay's FY2025 Form 10-K names Amazon, Alibaba, Alphabet (Google), Apple and Meta as larger competitors with broad ecosystems and greater resources.

The same 10-K identifies sellers' alternatives as general e-commerce marketplaces Amazon and Alibaba, specialized category marketplaces, and multi-channel services like Shopify or social media platforms.
The 10-K lists buyers' alternatives including Facebook Marketplace, Google Shopping, Instagram and TikTok shopping, plus live-commerce ventures and offline/online retailers.

Amazon is the dominant U.S. marketplace with an estimated $300 billion in third-party sales — more than seven times eBay's — while Temu, TikTok Shop and Walmart compete in a tight $15–22 billion range.
eBay holds the #2 position among U.S. marketplaces at an estimated $39 billion in GMV after refocusing on enthusiasts and pre-loved fashion.
Specialist marketplaces compete with eBay in its focus categories: Wayfair (~$10B, home goods), SHEIN marketplace (~$6B), Etsy (~$6B, handmade/vintage) and Whatnot (~$6B, live auctions).

ECDB's similarity ranking of eBay's top competitors (2025 GMV): Temu 87% match ($92.5B), Walmart.com 83% ($170.4B), Amazon.com 81% ($441.0B), TikTok Shop 79% ($64.4B), AliExpress 77% ($66.8B); eBay itself ~$37.5B.
